Hi all — quick update and practical workaround while we investigate root cause.

Observed likely causes:
- Okta SSO NameID mapping: if the incoming SAML NameID matches an existing external identity we treat it as an account link rather than new-account flow.
- Email normalization/subaddressing (user+tag@ vs user@) can make two representations of same mailbox; our accept flow currently rejects if it finds an existing username tied to a different inbound assertion.

Short-term (try these):
1) Laura — ask Sarah/Mark to open the invite link in an incognito window (or a different browser) and try the 'Create account' flow instead of 'Sign in with SSO' — sometimes the client cookies cause the route to skip the rebind.
2) If that fails, have them try accepting with a temporary personal email (e.g. sap+acme_temp@domain) so we can complete the onboarding and then manually reassign the org membership.

Longer-term fix: portal team needs to support an 'override-create' flag when an invite is accepted if the incoming NameID resolves to a different external identity. I filed a ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PORTAL-483 and added logs from the invite (attached).

Ops asks for engineering:
- Check the invite token metadata for the two invite emails (I see invite-eml.eml attached) and confirm whether the token contains the 'linked_identity' field.
- If linked_identity exists, options are (a) nuke the link and resend, (b) allow override-create for vendor invites, or (c) provide a clear error page explaining account rebind steps.

Laura — can you confirm whether Sarah or Mark are trying from a corporate-managed browser/device? If yes, incognito may work around SSO cookies but we might need a manual unlink.

I'll escalate to portal ops and request the unlink if needed.
